education.interpretation: Studying for exams that are coming up, comparing a longer daily routine with the current one.

branches.name: Study two hours daily
branches.description: You lengthen your daily study time.

branches.name: Keep one hour daily
branches.description: You carry on with your current routine.

variables.label: Study hours per day
variables.why: How long you study each day.

variables.label: Revision style
variables.why: How the study time is used.

questions: How many subjects do the exams cover?

formulas.label: Total study hours
formulas.explanation: Hours per day times the days in those weeks.

possibilities.text: More topics could be covered before the exams
Tiredness could build up in the last weeks
A steadier routine could leave room for other commitments
Some topics could be left for the final days

missingEvidence: How the marks are split between topics
limitations: Counts study time only, not how well the time is used.

projects.interpretation: A college moving from written exams to team-based projects, compared with keeping written exams.

branches.name: Team projects replace exams
branches.description: Assessment is done through projects completed in teams.

variables.label: How teams are formed
variables.why: Who is in each team could change the experience.

variables.label: Individual contribution is assessed
variables.why: Fairness depends on how each person's part is seen.

questions: How would each student's own contribution be judged?

possibilities.text: Teamwork skills could be practised more
Some students could carry more of the work than others
Results could stay easy to compare across students
Exam stress could remain high for some students

missingEvidence: How other colleges handled the change
limitations: Cannot say how students would actually respond.
